stem: A client taking digoxin has a serum digoxin concentration of 1.5 ng/mL drawn at least 6 hours after the last dose. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: Interpret the 1.5-ng/mL level as proof of toxicity and give digoxin immune Fab regardless of symptoms, renal function, or electrolyte status.
options.B: Interpret the 1.5-ng/mL level as subtherapeutic and automatically increase the dose without considering the indication or clinical response.
options.C: Interpret the 1.5-ng/mL level in the overall clinical context, including symptoms, renal function, electrolytes, indication, and response, rather than labeling the isolated value automatically therapeutic or toxic.
options.D: Ignore when the level was drawn because the interval between the last digoxin dose and specimen collection does not affect interpretation.

rationale: The current DailyMed digoxin label states that serum levels below 0.5 ng/mL have been associated with diminished efficacy and levels above 2 ng/mL with increased toxicity without increased benefit. It specifically instructs clinicians to interpret a serum digoxin concentration in the overall clinical context and not to use an isolated value alone to increase or decrease the dose. Levels should be obtained just before the next dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose. Therefore C is correct.
educational_objective: Interpret a properly timed digoxin concentration within the full clinical context and avoid making dose or toxicity decisions from an isolated serum value alone.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
source_version_date: Current DailyMed prescribing information; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: §2.5 Monitoring to Assess Safety, Efficacy, and Therapeutic Blood Levels: monitor toxicity and clinical response; <0.5 ng/mL associated with diminished efficacy; >2 ng/mL associated with increased toxicity; interpret concentration in overall clinical context; do not use an isolated measurement alone; collect just before next dose or at least 6 hours after last dose.
source_claim_supported: A serum digoxin concentration of 1.5 ng/mL drawn at least 6 hours after the dose should be interpreted with clinical response and toxicity assessment rather than automatically classified as therapeutic or toxic from the isolated number.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13: monitor diagnostic-test results, perform focused assessment, recognize trends/changes, and evaluate client responses to treatment.
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — therapeutic drug monitoring and digoxin toxicity risk

correction_summary: Retained key C, reverified the exact §2.5 concentration and timing language, added indication to the clinical-context interpretation, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests application of a direct label-monitoring principle.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed digoxin label; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: DailyMed §2.5; NCSBN Reduction of Risk Potential p.13 screenshot verified
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item preserves the label's numerical risk context, proper specimen timing and explicit warning against isolated-number dose decisions.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because 1.5 ng/mL alone does not establish toxicity or an indication for Fab.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because 1.5 ng/mL is not automatically subtherapeutic and dose changes cannot be based on the isolated number alone.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because specimen timing materially affects interpretation and the label specifies pre-dose or at least 6 hours post-dose sampling.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C incorporates both proper timing and the required clinical-context interpretation.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives interpret the same serum level and require label-based monitoring knowledge.
audit_findings.blueprint: Reduction of Risk Potential — laboratory interpretation and complication monitoring.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the exact DailyMed §2.5 text and rendered NCSBN p.13 page; rechecked all options, rationale, timing, concentration thresholds and Fab overstatement. C remained uniquely correct.
